item.text:
**6B.2, 2024: partial targeted support, but no broad improvement**
Putin’s 2024 record contains real welfare measures for families, disabled children, health care, and housing costs. But the clearest evidence on basic services is still negative in occupied/war-affected areas, and the positive evidence is narrow, targeted, and often tied to regime legitimacy.

| Stance | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Support | State guarantees of free medical care for 2024-2026 | Government of Russia | 2024-01-09 | https://government.ru/news/50600/ | The government approved a 2024-2026 program guaranteeing free medical care, including high-tech and specialized treatment. This is real access expansion in health care. | 6B.2, 5B.6, 6B.1 |
| Support | Nationwide support for families with three or more children | Government of Russia | 2024-01-25 | https://government.ru/en/news/50700/ | Putin made large-family support uniform nationwide, reducing regional variation in a concrete social benefit. This is limited but real social protection. | 6B.2, 5B.8, 6B.1 |
| Support | Expanded support for citizens caring for disabled people | Government of Russia | 2024-02-08 | https://government.ru/news/50822/ | Caregivers of disabled children kept monthly benefits even if they took jobs. That improves access to social protection for a vulnerable group. | 6B.2, 5B.8, 6B.1 |
| Support | Housing and utilities subsidies without bank commission for vulnerable groups | Government of Russia | 2024-04-30 | https://government.ru/docs/51490/ | Selected groups could pay housing and коммунальные services without bank fees. That is a small but concrete easing of housing-related costs. | 6B.2, 5B.8, 5B.6 |
| Support | Extended mortgage support for large families | Government of Russia | 2024-07-31 | https://government.ru/news/52275/ | The state extended large-family mortgage support for another seven years. This is direct housing assistance, though narrow and family-targeted. | 6B.2, 5B.8, 5B.6 |
| Support | Pilot project expanded rehabilitation for children with disabilities | Government of Russia | 2024-12-09 | https://government.ru/docs/53649/ | The pilot widened access to rehabilitation services for disabled children across more regions. This is one of the clearest 2024 health/social-protection improvements. | 6B.2, 5B.6, 5B.8 |
| Against | UN report details ‘climate of fear’ in occupied areas of Ukraine | United Nations in Ukraine | 2024-03-20 | https://ukraine.un.org/en/264055-un-report-details-%E2%80%98climate-fear%E2%80%99-occupied-areas-ukraine-russian-federation-moves-cement | The UN said Russia imposed its curriculum and institutions in occupied areas while denying healthcare and social security to people who refused Russian passports. That is direct evidence against improved access. | 6B.2, 5B.8, 5B.9 |
| Against | Two-year update. Protection of civilians: impact of hostilities on civilians since 24 February 2022 | United Nations in Ukraine | 2024-02-21 | https://ukraine.un.org/en/261245-two-year-update-protection-civilians-impact-hostilities-civilians-24-february-2022 | The UN said millions lost homes or access to basic services, and schools, medical facilities, and energy/grain infrastructure were damaged or destroyed. That is strong evidence of worsening access under Putin’s war. | 6B.2, 5B.9, 5B.10 |
| Against | Russia’s economy shows solid growth despite Ukraine war sanctions | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-28 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/russian-economy-shows-solid-growth-despite-ukraine-war-sanctions-3591756 | Reuters said much of the growth and low unemployment came from military production. That suggests the economy was not primarily improving access to civilian basics. | 6B.2, 5B.6, 5B.9, 5B.10 |
| Against | Russia prepares for further tax rises due to war | Ukrinform / Reuters | 2024-11-02 | https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/3922326-russia-prepares-for-further-tax-rises-due-to-war-reuters.html | Reuters’ reporting said war costs were forcing tax rises and cuts in small-business support and education development. That points to crowding out, not broad improvement in basic services. | 6B.2, 5B.6, 5B.9, 5B.10 |

Search gap: I found meaningful support for health care, housing costs, and social protection, but very little convincing 2024 evidence of broad improvements in water, sanitation, or food security. The strongest evidence on those basics is negative and comes from wartime/occupied territories, where access deteriorated sharply rather than improved.
